title: The model method: bar models for word problems
subject: math

items.prompt: Sam draws a bar model for 1 unit and 2 units. He draws the unit boxes in any lengths he likes, guessing the sizes, so his 2-unit bar is not twice his 1-unit bar. What is wrong with Sam's model?
items.answer: The unit boxes are not all the same length, so the bars are not to scale
choices: Nothing: a bar model is only a rough sketch
The colours of the bars are different
The unit boxes are not all the same length, so the bars are not to scale
Bar models must always use 7 units
items.misconceptionCode: Drawing unit boxes in any lengths, guessing the sizes.

items.prompt: Mia has 2 units and Ben has 3 units. Every unit box is drawn the same length. How many more units does Ben have than Mia?
Mia has 3 units. She gives 1 unit away to her sister. Draw a before-and-after model in your head: how many units does Mia have left?
A bar is split into 5 equal units. 2 units are red and the rest are blue. How many units are blue, and what is the difference between the blue units and the red units?
Which drawing is a correct bar model for 1 unit and 2 units?
items.answer: A 2-unit bar made of two unit boxes, each exactly the same length as the 1-unit bar
choices: A 2-unit bar drawn a little bit longer than the 1-unit bar
A 2-unit bar drawn three times as long as the 1-unit bar
A 2-unit bar made of two unit boxes, each exactly the same length as the 1-unit bar

items.prompt: Explain in one sentence why every unit box in a bar model must be the same length.
items.answer: Every unit box must be exactly the same length: two units is exactly twice one unit.
